Game of Thrones fans question cast about female violence at Comic-Con

Game of Thrones is based on the book series A Song of Ice and Fire, and in it, a lot of violence against women does occur. This is because it's set in the medieval period when women were treated like property. Cersei's walk actually happened in the book. At the same time, much of what went on in the show did NOT occur in the book. Robb's wife never died, for example. Sansa is tucked away in the Vale, and her friend is the one who gets assaulted. This is still violence, but we're less connected to the character. Shireen's death hasn't happened yet, but it's heavily implied it will.

The thing that is really appalling is that the show runners are notorious for cutting out strong moments from women. For example, Lady Stoneheart, the real story of Lyanna Stark, and Princess Arianne Martell. If you had these stories to balance out the horrible moments, it would be equivalent to the balance found between the horrors they inflict on the male characters and their moments of strength. Not to mention, Game of Thrones robs us of the happy moments that we see in A Song of Ice and Fire. Everything is tragic and dark 100% of the time in the show, whereas in the books there are moments of happiness. Little bits, but they are there.

I have some friends who play, but no one that plays regularly. One thing I have noticed about lots of established games is that the "new players areas" are abandoned because everyone is running end game content. Is worth it to start playing now?
Thinking of starting to play (yeah, I am a few years late to the game). Is it friendly to lowbie characters?
Definitely. Low level zones are still populated, and this game has one of the best communities around. People are always available to help out in-game.
People are key here. IMO Guild Wars 2 is way more enjoyable with other people, especially friends.

GW2 is the most friendly to lowbies because of how their scaling system works.

When you go to a zone that's lower than your level, you get automatically scaled down to the zone level, BUT the loot you get from doing activities there is relevant to your real level. That way people are encouraged to play everywhere all the time so it's not like other games where low level zones become ghost towns over time.

Also the open tag on all mobs and resources and quest items being shared make it so there's no competition for those and no ninja stealing can ever happen. That way people are more friendlier to each other, they are also rewarded for helping each other out.

It is indeed very noob friendly. There will be tutorials for very easy things such as dodging (pressing any direction key twice). Low leves zones are still populated thanks to the mega servers, which works like servers tied together. But also because of the level scaling in zones. If you're going to play guild wars 2, now is the time. Everyone is waiting for the expansion to hit you have plenty of time to catch up and even gear up. I think it's definitely worth to start playing now.
